summary: Describes an architecture for extending pseudowire emulation across multiple packet switched network segments, including cases where each segment belongs to a different provider. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A long pretend cable can be made of shorter pieces joined end to end, even if different companies own pieces.

questions: what is the difference between t-pe and s-pe
why use ms-pw instead of ss-pw
subtitle: How a pseudowire can be built from several linked segments instead of one end-to-end tunnel.

tldr.problem: Single-segment pseudowires need a full mesh of tunnels and signaling sessions between edge devices, which grows with the square of the number of devices and cannot cross routing domains or providers easily.
tldr.mechanism: A multi-segment pseudowire (MS-PW) chains two or more PW segments. Switching PEs (S-PEs) swap the PW label between segments, so the end devices (T-PEs) still see one point-to-point PW.
tldr.outcome: The RFC gives an Informational architecture covering reference models, control plane, management, congestion and security. It leaves wire encapsulations and setup mechanisms to other documents.

facts.label: Mesh growth
facts.value: Grows in proportion to the square of the number of PEs

today: RFC 5659 is an Informational document and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It sets out an architecture only; wire encapsulations and detailed setup mechanisms are non-goals of the document.

sections.title: Why Multi-Segment Pseudowires
sections.content:
RFC 3985 defines pseudowires (PWs) that begin and end on the edge of one packet switched network (PSN) with the PW label unchanged; these are now called single-segment pseudowires (SS-PWs). RFC 5659 extends the architecture so that point-to-point PWs can pass through multiple PSN tunnels. These are multi-segment pseudowires (MS-PWs), whose use cases and requirements are in RFC 5254.

Three problems drive this: keeping the density of the tunnel mesh down when PEs number in the hundreds or thousands, providing PWs across multiple routing domains or areas within one provider, and providing PWs across multiple providers and different PSN types. With a full mesh, the number of PEs, tunnels and signaling adjacencies grows in proportion to the square of the number of PEs. Switching PWs at an intermediate PE lets small edge devices keep a single adjacency, and lets many PWs share a few core tunnels.
sections.eli5: Instead of running a private wire between every pair of houses, you run wires to a few switching stations and join them. Each house still thinks it has one wire to its friend.

sections.title: T-PEs, S-PEs and Segments
sections.content:
A T-PE (terminating provider edge) is where the customer-facing attachment circuits (ACs) bind to a PW forwarder; it is present in the first and last segments of an MS-PW. An S-PE (switching provider edge) switches the control and data planes of the preceding and succeeding PW segments, terminating the PSN tunnels of both. A PW segment is the part of a PW that crosses one PSN tunnel in each direction. A PW switching point is never the S-PE and the T-PE for the same MS-PW.

From the point of view of a Layer 2 VPN, an MS-PW is indistinguishable from an SS-PW. The RFC notes that S-PEs were first expected only at provider edges, but the name stuck even though they can sit anywhere a PW must be processed or policy applied. Both directions of an MS-PW must traverse the same set of S-PEs, though the PSN tunnels between them might not follow reciprocal paths.
sections.eli5: The two end stations are where customers plug in. The stations in the middle only pass the call along from one cable to the next and never look at what is being said.

sections.title: Reference Models and Forwarding
sections.content:
In the reference model, a PSN tunnel runs from T-PE1 to S-PE1 across PSN1 and another from S-PE1 to T-PE2 across PSN2. Each PW segment on the first tunnel is switched to a segment on the second at S-PE1, the PW switching point. Segments of the same MS-PW must be of equivalent PW types, while the PSN tunnels may be of the same or different types. Encapsulations defined for SS-PWs are used without change.

The RFC describes intra-provider and inter-provider cases. In each, switching can happen using ACs (the PW reverts to the native service at the boundary and joins a separate PW) or using PWs (segments are switched without reverting to the native service). Inter-provider boundaries may also need per-PW OAM, Authentication, Authorization and Accounting (AAA), and security mechanisms.

At an S-PE, the forwarder picks the egress segment from the ingress PW label, with the mapping statically or dynamically configured. There is no native service processing in S-PEs. If both PSNs are the same type, such as MPLS, a simple label swap is done. If they differ, such as MPLS and L2TPv3, the ingress PW demultiplexer is popped, mapped, and the egress one pushed. Policies such as admission control, rate control, QoS mappings and security may be applied here.
sections.eli5: At each switching station, the label on a parcel is peeled off and replaced with the label for the next leg. The contents are never opened.

sections.title: Control Plane and Maintenance
sections.content:
Switching points may be statically provisioned or chosen dynamically. For static ones, PW labels can be set by configuration or signaled per segment, so one MS-PW can mix configured and signaled segments. For dynamic choice, either the T-PEs determine the full path, or each T-PE and S-PE makes a local next-hop decision using configured information or a dynamic path-selection mechanism.

An emulated service can only be considered up when every PW segment and PSN tunnel along the path works, in both directions if the service is bi-directional. If a failure notification mechanism exists across consecutive segments, the S-PE must propagate the notifications. A PW-TYPE identifier exchanged at setup helps detect misconnection and payload type mismatch, and end-to-end connection verification can check the identity of S-PEs and the far T-PE.

For management, each S-PE is a new point where defects may occur, so troubleshooting should work on a subset of segments as well as edge to edge, and should verify which S-PEs a path traverses. Remote management may need to operate securely across provider boundaries.
sections.eli5: The path can be set up by hand or worked out on the fly. The whole line counts as working only if every piece works, and tools should be able to test one piece at a time.

sections.title: Congestion and Security
sections.content:
Congestion in the data plane can degrade the control plane, since they fate-share in traditional IP networks. Inter-provider MS-PWs make it hard to guarantee a PW will not congest a downstream PSN, so each segment needs congestion detection and control where capacity cannot be provisioned in advance. T-PEs likely hold the information needed to apply control fairly, so S-PEs need to propagate congestion state in both directions, while an S-PE at the border of a congested PSN can respond faster. QoS treatment at an S-PE can come from signaled PW parameters or from fields such as the TC bits of an MPLS label or the DS field of an L2TPv3 outer IP header.

On security, RFC 3985 applies, and detailed requirements are in RFC 5254. S-PEs expose the PW label to extra processing, and an implicit trust relationship exists between the initiator, the T-PEs and the S-PEs. An S-PE should not pick a next hop unless it would be considered eligible by the originator. Directly connecting border devices over a physically secure link with signaling and routing authentication removes the chance of receiving signaling from an untrusted peer. Peer entity authentication should be used between providers, and S-PEs that also act as T-PEs need mechanisms so an MS-PW is not switched into a local AC.
sections.eli5: Because many companies share the road, each stretch needs to watch for traffic jams and tell its neighbors. Each station should also make sure the next one is someone it trusts.
